Model assumptions

data/assumptions.json

NumberValueSourceLinks
rentSupplyElasticity -0.1 Li (2022), "Do New Housing Units in Your Backyard Raise Your Rents?", Journal of Economic Geography: a 10% increase in housing stock within 500 ft lowers rents 1%.

Alternate: -0.19. Mense (2025), Journal of Political Economy Macroeconomics: 1% new housing supply lowers average rent 0.19%.
propertyTaxRate 0.005 Town of Chapel Hill FY2025-26 property tax rate: 50.0 cents per $100 of assessed value.
canopyMinPct low_res 0.4 · mid_res 0.3 · mixed_use 0.2 · parking 0.2 · transit_station 0.2 Chapel Hill Land Use Management Ordinance (LUMO) Section 5.7: tree canopy minimums of 20-40%.

Which value in that range applies to each zone state is our mapping, not the ordinance's. Forest counts as full canopy.
unitsPerAcre forest 0 · low_res 4 · mid_res 15 · mixed_use 70 · parking 0 · transit_station 0 Town of Chapel Hill Future Land Use Map, "Charting Our Future" (Dec 2020): Low Residential 1-4 units/acre, High Residential 8-15+,; last codified LUMO Table 3.8-1 density caps (R-2 4.0, R-5 and R-6 15.0),; approved mixed-use projects: Fordham Blvd Apartments (Chapelboro, 2017-05-09), Aura Blue Hill (News & Observer, 2021-10-28), 101 E. Rosemary St (Town staff report, 2023)

Which district stands for which zone state is our mapping. mixed_use 70 is the low end of three approved Chapel Hill projects (about 70, 99 and 214 units/acre, our calculation); a suburban-village style (MU-V arterial cap) would be about 20. Chapel Hill removed its residential density caps in 2023 (Ord. 2023-06-21/O-6).

commuteDistancePenalty 0.6 minutes ACS 2020-2024 5-year: mean travel time = B08013 (aggregate minutes) / B08303 (workers who did not work from home), by census tract. and

Our calculation: map_edge zones, assigned to tracts by centroid and weighted by acres, average 20.1 min vs 19.5 town-wide. That is inside the tracts' margins of error, so statistically indistinguishable from 0. Used by the aggregate sim; the page's commute comes from the household model.

agentHouseholds downtown 105 · campus 98 · edge 97 · corridor 0 PLACEHOLDER needs citation

Simulated households per zone at year 0. From the household-model prototype.
agentUnits downtown 108 · campus 101 · edge 100 · corridor 0 PLACEHOLDER needs citation

Simulated homes per zone at year 0. Homes the zone rules build are added by parcel: corridor parcels to corridor, other map_edge parcels to edge, the rest to downtown. CH-LUTI's other new homes are added by its zone: downtown and north to downtown, campus to campus, east and south (which commute over 15-501) to edge. From the household-model prototype.
agentBurdenLine 0.3 U.S. Census Bureau ACS 2020-2024 5-year, B25070 "Gross Rent as a Percentage of Household Income", Chapel Hill town, which reports renters paying 30% or more; HUD counts households paying more than 30% of income for housing as cost-burdened.

Rent share of income above which burden that builds up after arrival counts toward leaving (see agentLeaveRate). The 30% line is the standard; using it in a leaving rule is our modelling choice.

 data.census.gov
agentLeaveRate 0.003 per point of burden, per year PLACEHOLDER needs citation

Each year a renter leaves with chance 1 - e^(-rate x points), counting only burden above 30% (agentBurdenLine) that has built up since they arrived: points above the higher of 30% and their burden on arrival. Rents follow CH-LUTI and incomes grow as CH-LUTI's do, so this is rent rising faster than income. Priced out counts year-0 households only; about 1 in 100 renters per 1% rent rise above no policy (tests/agents.test.js).

lutiRegionalGrowth lo 0.0035 · mid 0.0073 · hi 0.015 /yr PLACEHOLDER lo and hi need citation. mid: U.S. Census Bureau decennial census households (occupied housing units), Chapel Hill town: 20,564 in 2010 (SF1 H3) and 22,118 in 2020 (P.L. 94-171 H1)

lutiHouseholdAdjust 0.25 PLACEHOLDER needs citation

Share of the gap between desired and actual households closed each quarter (leases turn over yearly). From the CH-LUTI model.
lutiMinVacancy 0.015 PLACEHOLDER needs citation

lutiIncomeGrowth 0.0275 /yr U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts, Chapel Hill town, North Carolina (ACS 5-year estimates): median gross rent $1,172 (2014-2018) and $1,483 (2019-2023); median household income $68,640 (2014-2018) and $85,825 (2019-2023).

Nominal household income growth, for rent burden in CH-LUTI and the household model. Our calculation: over those five years rent grew 4.82%/yr and income 4.57%/yr, so incomes trailed rents by 0.25 points a year. CH-LUTI's rent path rises with rentDrift (3%/yr at its central value, Zillow ZORI), so incomes grow 3% - 0.25 points = 2.75%/yr.

federalStandardDeduction single 16100 · joint 32200 $ (2026) IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32, inflation adjustments for tax year 2026.

Year 0 is 2026. Take-home pay is wages less federal and North Carolina income tax and payroll tax, with the standard deduction and no credits (such as the child tax credit). Students, single renters and "You" file single; families and owners file jointly (data/residents.json). Later years index every dollar threshold with rent inflation (CH-LUTI's rentDrift).

ceTotalSpending 16658 35046 · 42925 50054 · 74474 66900 · 121548 89972 · 264510 150342 average income before taxes of each quintile -> yearly total expenditures, both in 2024 $ BLS Consumer Expenditure Surveys 2024, quintiles of income before taxes (released December 19, 2025), via FRED series CXUTOTALEXPLB0102M-0106M; the keys are each quintile's average income before taxes (CXUINCBEFTXLB0102M-0106M).

Other spending (everything but housing and the commute) is what a household of the same income spends in the CE: its after-tax income x (1 - personalSavingRate), times the share of CE spending, less personal insurance and pensions, that is neither shelter nor the commute: (total - insurance and pensions - shelter - commuteShareOfDriving x transportation) / (total - insurance and pensions). The share (about 0.69-0.71) is interpolated on year-0 income between the quintiles (flat beyond the end ones). A household whose rent takes a typical share saves about the national saving rate; one whose rent takes more falls short. Set in year 0, it grows with rent inflation (CH-LUTI's rentDrift).

startingSavings 0 900 · 29932 2600 · 57452 7100 · 94511 15700 · 155925 33700 lower bound of income before taxes (2024 $) -> savings ($, 2022) Federal Reserve, 2022 Survey of Consumer Finances, Table 6 (family holdings of financial assets): median transaction accounts (checking, savings, money market) of families holding them, by percentile of income: less than 20th 900, 20-39.9 2,600, 40-59.9 7,100, 60-79.9 15,700, 80-89.9 33,700.; quintile lower bounds from BLS Consumer Expenditure Surveys 2024 (29,932 / 57,452 / 94,511 / 155,925).

Savings at the start of year 0, by the income quintile of the household's year-0 income, in year-0 dollars. The top quintile takes the 80-89.9 median, not the 90-100 one ($111,100), as no showcase household is near the 90th percentile. No interest. Savings never go below zero: a shortfall after they are gone is bills falling behind.
